summary: Periodic scans can create alert fatigue, delayed detection and large unowned repair batches; continuous or event-driven controls may be better for fast-moving risks.

points.text: A weekly or monthly schedule leaves a known exposure window; critical advisory, credential and policy events need immediate triggers rather than waiting for cron.
Repeatedly reporting the same accepted debt inflates dashboards and teaches teams to ignore the sweep unless fingerprints, suppressions and expiry are first-class.
Whole-repository analysis can consume substantial CI capacity and model budget, especially when every run re-analyzes unchanged components.
Batching findings into scheduled campaigns creates larger, riskier remediation changes than continuously updating small dependencies or constraints.
